prompt: What is supply-side policy?

options.label: B

options.label: C

options.label: D
options.text: Measures changing only the exchange rate

explanation: Supply-side policy aims to improve the economy's ability to produce. In AD/AS terms, successful measures increase long-run aggregate supply rather than merely changing aggregate demand.

options.label: D

options.label: C

options.label: D

prompt: A successful supply-side policy raises labour productivity and real output. What can be concluded about employment from these changes alone?

options.label: A
options.text: Employment falls whenever output per worker rises

options.label: B
options.text: Employment is fixed

options.label: C
options.text: Employment depends on relative growth rates

options.label: D
options.text: Employment rises whenever real output rises, regardless of changes in productivity

explanation: Employment is related to output divided by output per worker. If productivity rises, a given output can be produced with fewer workers; whether employment rises depends on how strongly output expands relative to productivity.

prompt: Which statement best describes the general price-level effect of a successful rightward aggregate-supply shift, with aggregate demand unchanged?

options.label: A

options.label: C
options.text: Prices tend to fall

options.label: D
options.text: Higher capacity makes firms raise their prices despite unchanged demand

explanation: With aggregate demand unchanged, a rightward supply shift reduces scarcity at each level of demand and tends to lower the equilibrium price level.

prompt: A factory employs 200 workers and produces 10 000 units per week. After a training programme it employs the same 200 workers and produces 11 500 units. What has happened to output per worker?

options.label: C
options.text: It has fallen from 57.5 to 50 units per worker

options.label: D
options.text: It is unchanged because employment is unchanged

explanation: Before training, output per worker is 10 000 / 200 = 50 units. Afterwards it is 11 500 / 200 = 57.5 units, so labour productivity has risen.

| B | vocational training | port expansion | technology grants |
| C | higher tariffs | import quota | embargo |
| D | higher consumption spending | lower interest rate | income transfer |

options.label: A
options.text: A

options.label: B
options.text: B

options.label: C
options.text: C

options.label: D
options.text: D

explanation: Package B combines training, infrastructure and support for technological improvement, all of which directly target productive capacity or productivity.

prompt:
The table gives output and employment before and after four programmes. Which programme produces the largest percentage increase in labour productivity?

| Programme | Output before | Workers before | Output after | Workers after |
| A | 2 000 | 100 | 2 150 | 100 |
| B | 3 000 | 120 | 3 120 | 120 |
| C | 1 600 | 80 | 1 840 | 80 |
| D | 2 500 | 100 | 2 625 | 100 |

options.label: A
options.text: Programme A

options.label: B
options.text: Programme C

options.label: C
options.text: Programme B

options.label: D
options.text: Programme D

explanation: Productivity is output per worker. A rises from 20 to 21.5 (+7.5%), B from 25 to 26 (+4%), C from 20 to 23 (+15%), and D from 25 to 26.25 (+5%). Programme C has the largest increase.
reference: 5.4 Supply-side policy | 5.4.2; 5.4.3 productivity objective and supply-side tools | AO2 Analysis

prompt: A government must choose between a one-year increase in transfer payments and a long-term programme of technical training, with equal initial budget cost. Which is more directly a supply-side measure?

options.label: A
options.text: Transfer payments, because any government spending shifts LRAS right

options.label: B
options.text: Transfer payments, because they directly increase worker skills

options.label: C
options.text: Neither, because government spending can never be supply-side

options.label: D
options.text: Technical training

explanation: Technical training is designed to improve productive skills. Transfer payments mainly redistribute income and are not, by themselves, a direct means of increasing productive capacity.
reference: 5.4 Supply-side policy | 5.4.3 tools of supply-side policy, for example training, infrastructure development, support for technological improvement | AO3 Evaluation

prompt: A country improves productivity substantially but its labour force shrinks at the same time. Which statement is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: Potential output must increase because productivity rose

options.label: B
options.text: Potential output must decrease because labour fell

options.label: C
options.text: LRAS cannot change when two determinants move in opposite directions

options.label: D
options.text: The potential-output effect is uncertain

explanation: Higher productivity raises potential output, while a smaller labour force reduces it. The net LRAS effect depends on the relative size of the two changes.
reference: 5.4 Supply-side policy | 5.4.2 objectives of supply-side policy: increasing productivity and productive capacity | AO3 Evaluation

prompt: A technology programme raises the efficiency of machines but firms do not adopt the technology because they lack skilled workers. What would most improve the policy package?

options.label: A
options.text: Complementary worker training

options.label: B
options.text: A policy that raises transport costs

options.label: C
options.text: A reduction in all vocational education

options.label: D
options.text: A measure that restricts firms from investing

explanation: Technology and human capital can be complementary. If skill shortages prevent adoption, targeted training increases the chance that technology support will translate into higher productivity.
reference: 5.4 Supply-side policy | 5.4.3 tools of supply-side policy, for example training, infrastructure development, support for technological improvement | AO3 Evaluation

prompt: The government builds a new motorway, but it largely duplicates an uncongested existing route. Which is the best evaluation?

options.label: A
options.text: A small gain if no important bottleneck is removed

options.label: B
options.text: All infrastructure spending shifts LRAS right by the same amount

options.label: C
options.text: The motorway must reduce labour productivity

options.label: D
options.text: The project becomes monetary policy because it is inefficient

explanation: Infrastructure raises productivity when it solves a real constraint. A duplicate route with little use may have a high opportunity cost and a small effect on productive capacity.
reference: 5.4 Supply-side policy | 5.4.3 tools of supply-side policy, for example training, infrastructure development, support for technological improvement | AO3 Evaluation

prompt: An economy initially has AD1, SRAS1 and LRAS1 intersecting at full-employment output Y1. A successful supply-side policy shifts SRAS and LRAS right while AD is unchanged. Which final combination is most likely?

options.label: A
options.text: Higher output, lower prices and higher capacity

options.label: B
options.text: Lower real output, higher price level and lower capacity

options.label: C
options.text: Unchanged output, higher price level and lower capacity

options.label: D
options.text: Higher real output, higher price level and lower capacity

explanation: A rightward shift of both short-run and long-run aggregate supply allows more output at a lower price level, while the LRAS shift shows that productive capacity has increased.
reference: 5.4 Supply-side policy | 5.4.1; 5.4.2; 5.4.4 LRAS, productive capacity and AD/AS impact | AO2 Analysis

prompt: A country has an inflationary output constraint caused by inadequate electricity supply to industry. Which policy best targets the cause?

options.label: A
options.text: A rise in the policy interest rate only

options.label: B
options.text: Reliable electricity infrastructure

options.label: C
options.text: A cut in worker training

options.label: D
options.text: A reduction in productive investment

explanation: If electricity capacity is the binding supply constraint, infrastructure investment directly addresses the bottleneck. Demand restraint may lower inflation but does not remove the productive constraint.
reference: 5.4 Supply-side policy | 5.4.3 tools of supply-side policy, for example training, infrastructure development, support for technological improvement | AO3 Evaluation

prompt: A government wants to reduce cost-push inflation over the long run without reducing productive capacity. Which approach is most suitable?

options.label: A
options.text: Measures that deliberately reduce worker skills

options.label: B
options.text: Raise productivity and reduce unit costs

options.label: C
options.text: Measures that raise transport costs

options.label: D
options.text: Measures that shrink the capital stock

explanation: Supply-side improvements can lower unit costs and shift aggregate supply right, reducing inflationary pressure while increasing rather than sacrificing productive capacity.
reference: 5.4 Supply-side policy | 5.4.2; 5.4.3; 5.4.4 productivity, tools and macroeconomic impact | AO3 Evaluation
graphDescription: AD/AS diagram: Price Level vertical; Real Output horizontal. AD is unchanged. A successful productivity policy shifts AS right and LRAS right, lowering cost pressure while expanding potential output.

graphScenes.caption: Schematic; labeled numbers specify quantitative values.

prompt: A country reduces corporation tax and increases training. Investment rises, but the training is poor quality. Which supply-side channel is most likely to remain effective?

options.label: A
options.text: Investment can still expand the capital stock

options.label: B
options.text: Both channels must fail because one programme is poor

options.label: C
options.text: Training quality determines whether private investment can occur at all

options.label: D
options.text: The policies must reduce LRAS because they are combined

explanation: Different supply-side tools work through different mechanisms. Weak training limits the human-capital effect, but stronger investment can still raise the capital stock and productive capacity.
reference: 5.4 Supply-side policy | 5.4.3 tools of supply-side policy, for example training, infrastructure development, support for technological improvement | AO3 Evaluation

prompt: Which statement must be true if a policy has shifted LRAS to the right?

options.label: A
options.text: Actual output must already equal the new potential output

options.label: B
options.text: Productive potential has increased

options.label: C
options.text: The price level must have fallen

options.label: D
options.text: AD must have increased

explanation: LRAS represents potential output. Its rightward shift therefore proves that productive capacity has increased, but says nothing definite about current AD, actual output or the price level.
reference: 5.4 Supply-side policy | 5.4.1; 5.4.2 LRAS meaning and productive-capacity objective | AO2 Analysis

prompt: Which package is least likely to be classified as supply-side policy?

options.label: A
options.text: Retraining, mobility support and apprenticeships

options.label: B
options.text: Ports, broadband and freight rail investment

options.label: C
options.text: Rate cuts, easier credit and money expansion

options.label: D
options.text: Technology grants and fewer regulations alongside incentives for firms to invest

explanation: Lower interest rates, easier credit and a larger money supply are monetary-policy tools aimed primarily at aggregate demand. The other packages target productive efficiency or capacity.
reference: 5.4 Supply-side policy | 5.4.3 tools of supply-side policy, for example training, infrastructure development, support for technological improvement | AO2 Analysis

prompt: A government introduces training, infrastructure development and technology support at the same time. What common mechanism justifies classifying all three as supply-side policies?

options.label: A
options.text: All reduce demand immediately

options.label: B
options.text: All alter only the budget balance without affecting production

options.label: C
options.text: All can expand resource productivity or capacity

options.label: D
options.text: All work exclusively by discouraging households from buying imported goods

explanation: Although the measures operate differently, each can improve the quantity, quality or effectiveness of productive resources and therefore raise LRAS.
reference: 5.4 Supply-side policy | 5.4.1; 5.4.2; 5.4.3 meaning, objectives and tools of supply-side policy | AO2 Analysis

prompt: A government combines high-quality retraining, a freight-network upgrade and support for firms adopting advanced machinery. Which outcome best indicates that the package has succeeded?

options.label: A
options.text: Productive capacity falls while price pressure rises

options.label: B
options.text: Higher productivity, potential output and LRAS

options.label: C
options.text: Worker skills fall and transport costs rise

options.label: D
options.text: LRAS shifts left even though resource quality improves

explanation: The package addresses human capital, infrastructure and technology. Success should be visible in higher productivity, greater productive capacity and a rightward LRAS shift; if current AS also rises, output can increase with less price pressure.
reference: 5.4 Supply-side policy | 5.4.1; 5.4.2; 5.4.3; 5.4.4 complete supply-side policy chain from tools to macroeconomic impact | AO3 Evaluation
